changes.comment: safer-fetch: new createGuardedFetch(options) returns a fetch-shaped GuardedFetch whose every request goes through the same hop walk as the buffered entry points (address guard on every hop, request guard, redirect policy defaulting to 'reject', loop detection, monotonic credential stripping, per-hop headers deadline) and whose response is returned with its body unread, so Server-Sent Events and MCP Streamable HTTP work through it. init.signal cancels guard evaluation, the connect, a redirect walk and the body after return. It rejects with the new GuardedFetchError, whose message is fixed text and whose reason is the FetchFailureReason. Options that need the body read or would retry (timeoutMs, maxResponseBytes, responseBodyGuard, retry) are refused at creation. Internally the hop walk is now shared between the buffered and streaming paths; the buffered entry points are unchanged, except that a call already stopped no longer starts a guard or transport call whose result it would discard. A binary request body is now copied before the first await — a Uint8Array or ArrayBuffer in createGuardedFetch, and a Uint8Array in the buffered entry points (which take string | Uint8Array) — so the bytes the guards approve are the bytes sent even if the caller mutates its buffer during the call. Every timeout and delay option that reaches a timer (timeoutMs and headersTimeoutMs on the buffered entry points, headersTimeoutMs on createGuardedFetch, retry.baseDelayMs and retry.maxDelayMs) is now refused above 2147483647 ms, the largest delay setTimeout honours; a larger value used to time out after 1 ms. New exports: the FetchFailureKind type (FetchFailureReason['kind']) and SAFER_FETCH_METHODS, the runtime list SaferFetchMethod is now derived from (the union is unchanged).
